_what: Every number the edit kit uses. Change a number here, never in edit.py. These are the settled rules of the edit line (cut and dress), brand-free.

canvas.what: 9:16 only. fps: the cut sheet's own fps wins; else the first clip's; else this

listen.what: silence is found in the SOUND, not in the words: anything quieter than -35 dB for 0.15 s or longer

cut.what: start and end silence always cut, leaving 0.10 s before the first sound and 0.14 s after the last. Gaps under 0.35 s are breaths and are always kept. Gaps of 0.35 s or more are mid-clip pauses: the kit proposes cutting them, the editor keeps any that land a beat (--keep).

punch.what: after a cut pause the next piece is 7% closer, so the jump reads like a second camera in the room. Zoom centre sits at 32% down the frame (face height).

cut_off.what: a talking clip whose sound is still going in its last 0.15 s probably stops mid-line: flagged, sent back to production, never edited around

level.what: each clip's sound is levelled to -16 LUFS before the cut, so scenes match

master.what: the finished file: -14 LUFS integrated, peaks no higher than -1 dBTP

safe.what: the 9:16 frame keeps everything that matters inside the centred 4:5 band (1080x1350 of 1080x1920): nothing above 14.84% or below 85.16%. The ui_* numbers are where the app's own buttons sit (organic feeds); text stays out of them.

zones.what: named text spots, % of the frame. All sit inside the 4:5 band and clear of the app buttons.

card.what: hook and cards: black heavy type on a white plate, the cut sheet's exact words and line breaks

looks.what: caption looks. Captions show 2-4 words at a time and the spoken word lights up; one line breaks on a pause of 0.35 s or more and on . ! ?

checks.what: final checks: no silence of 0.7 s or more anywhere in the master; no black frames; the file is 9:16
